newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ABN AMRO MULLS MEESPIERSON SALE.
newsitem.headline: ABN AMRO MULLS MEESPIERSON SALE.

text.p: Dutch bank ABN AMRO NV said on Tuesday it would sell its MeesPierson investment banking unit under the right circumstances in a disposal which analysts believe could raise up to 2.0 billion guilders.
The bank earlier announced it was holding discussions after being approached by a number of unnamed parties interested in buying MeesPierson, which is currently being restructured.
ABN AMRO spokesman Jules Prast said the announcement was made because rumours had started in financial markets.
Analysts said Dutch-Belgian insurer Fortis Amev was rumoured to be a possible buyer.
But a Fortis Amev spokesman said: "We don't comment on individual (cases)."
There has long been speculation that ABN AMRO would sell MeesPierson but the Dutch bank had always responded that it was not for sale.
"The implication of this (announcement) is that yes, under circumstances, it would be for sale," Prast told Reuters, but he declined to name the parties involved in the talks.
Hans Pluijgers of Kempen and Co said ABN AMRO had been restructuring MeesPierson to focus more on investment banking and less on commercial banking.
"It must be worth about 2.0 billion guilders," he added.
CS First Boston analyst Mark Hoge said he was not surprised at the announcement as MeesPierson's return on capital was below ABN AMRO's targets.
He said the wholly-owned subsidiary also replicated the activities of its parent in some areas.
"They would be happy if they could just get out of it," Hoge said.
He said ABN AMRO would be happy to recover book value of just under 2.0 billion guilders.
